title: 16th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The 16th sitting opened at 09:02 on 5 November 2025 under Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla. MPs first debated the Velidhoo member's resolution calling on the government not to allow shark fishing: the proposer argued it would harm diving tourism and the reef ecosystem, while most other speakers opposed it, citing fishers' livelihoods and regulated, monitored fishing. They then debated the Kendhoo member's resolution on delays in handing over flats under the Gedhoruveriya housing scheme, with government-aligned members saying handover is on track and others urging speed. After a recess (10:30 to 11:01) debate began on a committee report on amendments to the Special Economic Zones Act; no votes were held in this part. The text is partly garbled, so figures such as attendance are read as printed. MPs debated a committee report on a bill to amend the Higher Education and Training Act (Law 2021/7). Three members spoke in favour, praising wider consultation and the chance for colleges to gain university status. The Majlis then held four votes: two member resolutions (on shark fishing and on delayed housing flats) were not accepted, while the Special Economic Zones Act amendment and the higher education amendment both passed. The sitting then closed.

Resolution on delays in handing over flats under the Gedhoruveriya and Binveriya housing projects (Kendhoo member)

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Proposed the shark resolution, saying shark fishing would hurt diving tourism, the reef food chain and shark numbers.
Said divers and dive operators had asked him to oppose shark fishing; said the resolution was not against fishers.
On the housing resolution, welcomed that recipients for the 4000 flats were chosen but urged meeting promised handover dates.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Opposed the shark resolution, saying it looked unresearched and that fish stocks exist for people to eat.
Pointed to vessel tracking and sustainable-fishing rules; a point of order from the proposer was upheld during his speech.
On housing, said the government is finishing and handing over flats, and complaints about allocations should be examined.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: On sharks, took no firm side; called for a scientific study, licensing and monitoring and said tourism should not be the only economy.
On housing, urged faster handover of the 4000 flats and publication of the recipients' list and criteria.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Did not support the shark resolution; said fishers face hardship and regulated, monitored fishing is possible alongside tourism.
As committee deputy chair, presented the report: wide consultation with universities, colleges and the ministry, site visits, and cross-party agreement on the changes.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Said critics calling the president's housing pledges false were wrong; the pledge was five years and work is under way.
Explained that flats were allocated by points under the 2023 announcement, with higher points getting three-bedroom flats.
Said flats are being finished before handover so residents avoid fit-out loans, with most handovers expected in November.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Opposed the shark resolution; said ordinary Maldivians need livelihoods beyond resort jobs and sea resources should be used sustainably.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Opposed the shark resolution; said shark fishing can be controlled under clear rules and that citizens who wish to do it should be allowed.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Opposed the shark resolution; said fishing was banned in 2010, northern fishers lost income, and offshore fishing does not affect tourism.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Said both fishing and tourism matter; asked members not to politicise the issue and to rely on study, regulation and the two ministries working together.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Proposed amendments on the health-centre definition, tourism-related taxes and ongoing projects; said MDP could revisit its vote if they were included.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Backed the bill; said special economic zones need special incentives to attract investment, existing projects should be covered, and PNC would support it.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the report; said the amendments set rules for higher education institutions and for colleges becoming universities.
Argued more local institutions would give Maldivian students more study options and attract foreign students.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Thanked the committee for its thorough work on the bill sent to it in July 2024.
Said it opens the way for more universities and gives well-run colleges a path to university status.

decisions: Debate on the Velidhoo member's shark resolution was closed; the vote was left for the day's vote hour.
Debate on the Kendhoo member's housing-flats resolution was closed without a closing reply because the proposer was absent; the vote was left for the vote hour.
The chair told the house that no member amendments had been received to the committee report on the Special Economic Zones Act amendment bill.
Resolution to allow shark catching and a shark fishery was not accepted by the Majlis.
Resolution on delayed handover of Gedhoruveriya and Binveriya flats was not accepted by the Majlis.
Special Economic Zones Act amendment bill (2014/24) passed.
Higher Education and Training Act amendment bill (2021/7) passed.

votes.what: Accept resolution on shark catching and shark fishery (Velidhoo member)
Accept resolution on delayed Gedhoruveriya/Binveriya flats (Kendhoo member)

Pass Higher Education and Training Act amendment bill (2021/7)
